pr.t: Silver Anniversary Celebrations, S. Africa Satsang Mandal
w: 113 devotees participated in a yagna for World Peace.

After having lunch, a kishore asked Swamishri, "Swami my mind wonders off while doing puja." Swamishri : "Have you seen a Chimpanzee?" Kishore: "Yes." Swamishri: "Well the mind is like a monkey. Whenever you sit down for devotion and bhajan the mind wanders off because one desires to see worldly things. The mind is maya. It will not sit down for the darshan of God but it will concentrate for hours while watching T.V. When you go to the mandir the mind feels like leaving immediately. The same applies when you are listening to a religious discourse. But while watching T.V, you sit for hours because you like it and appreciate it. Similarly, when you start liking God and Satsang, then your mind will not wander off and desire to see and experience worldly things." Kishore: "How can we always have divyabhav (divine feelings) for you?" Swamishri: "When you understand the glory then you will experience divine feelings. We love our friends and know their greatness so we never find faults in them. Because you have understood the glory of friendship you don’t feel bad or find fault even when your friends scold you. Likewise, if you realise the glory of God and His holy sadhu you will never find faults in them."
Sunday, 7 August 2005 (Shravan sud 2, Samvat 2061), Bochasan

At 11.00 am Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the assembly. Mahant Swami was speaking beautifully on "nishtha" (firm faith). Turning his mala, Swamishri listened to the talk. After his discourse, Nehal Chudasama, who had come from the UK, sang the kirtan "Je dukh thay te thajo re..." (Let whatever pain come). Blessing them, Swamishri said, "Wonderful! These boys have come from America and London, and they sang this kirtan! We keep them seated here and look after them, so they stay seated, but if anything goes even slightly wrong right now, they will be off to America. Here there is only a little hardship, yet instead of company with the sadhus there would be a great commotion. If that happened, the singing would be wasted. So since you have sung this, keep it always. All kinds of hardships will come, but the mind should not hold back from worshipping God. In worldly dealings, in family life, thousands of kinds of hardship come, yet we stay put. If husband and wife quarrel, they bear with each other. A husband and wife quarrelled, and everyone asked what happened. The wife said, 'My tongue moved, so his hand moved.' So in worldly life we adjust our minds. In satsang, if someone says even a little something, people go back home. At home there is so much hardship, wife and children speak, the government and parents speak, yet we do not consider that suffering. Here, in worshipping God, we consider it suffering.

"The kirtan says, 'Let whatever pain come in worshipping God...', because God has not come to give pain. God gives pain to test the devotee. One who is studying is tested. In the same way God also tests to see whether the devotee is true or just for show."
Sunday, 7 August 2005 (Vikram Samvat 2061, Shravan sud 2), Bochasan

Sixty BAPS teenagers and 50 children and teenage girls of UK arrived in Atladra after completing their pilgrimage of holy places in Gujarat and Chhapaiya. They were to spend a week to avail of Swamishri’s blessings and spiritual company. Swamishri blessed them during a special assembly, “In your age you can attain a lot and you can also lose a lot. If you get into bad company you lose out, and if you come to satsang then you will be liberated. If you associate with good people, read good things, see good things then you will be liberated. But if you sit with wrong people then you will get drowned. When anyone gets involved with kusang then he will lose interest in satsang.” Swamishri blessed them for 50 minutes.

The mahapuja for the foundation-stone laying ceremony for the BAPS shikharbaddh mandir in Dhari commenced soon after the mangala arti. Senior sadhus and leading devotees from Dhari participated in the rituals. After completing his morning puja Swamishri performed the pujan rituals of all the foundation stones, three kalashas, Kurma, Anant and Bhumi. He showered rose petals on the stones and placed the asthi of Yogiji Maharaj. [The ritual on site in Dhari was performed by senior sadhus on 17 October.]
Today Phuleshbhai phoned from South Africa. He said, "Today is Raksha Bandhan, so please tell me some seva for this day."
Mahant Swami Maharaj said, "You already have a big seva in the South Africa mandir!"
He said, "Yes. But please say something so that today will be memorable."
He wanted it so much that Swamishri laughed and said, "500 rand."
As soon as Swamishri said this, Phuleshbhai exclaimed with great joy, "Oh Swami! You even remember that the currency here is the rand!"
Phuleshbhai and the sadhus too were greatly impressed by Swamishri's sharp memory.

Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the night session of the shibir. This session was the "Iti Vachanamrutam" dialogue. As at every centre, the volunteers took their places before Swamishri here too. A volunteer dressed as the presenter began reading the Vachanamrut.

"Swaminarayan Hare, Vachanamrut Chino Hills section 1: on fortune awakening." Then, continuing in the style of the Vachanamrut, the volunteers asked Swamishri one interesting question after another, and Swamishri gave very beautiful answers.
Question 1: How should we take the Satsang Shikshan Pariksha with an understanding of its glory?

Swamishri said, "The Satsang Shikshan Pariksha... it contains what is worth knowing to go to Akshardham. Nothing else you know will be of any use. Decide whether you want to go to Akshardham or keep going round in circles here."
Question 2: We get bored preparing for the Satsang Shikshan Pariksha. The mind does not stay focused. We get busy in worldly work. So what is the remedy?

Swamishri said, "The Satsang Shikshan Pariksha is worth billions of rupees, and any worldly work, however important, is worth half a rupee or a rupee. Let us understand this glory, because what is our attainment? The fruit of the Satsang Shikshan Pariksha is Akshardham."
Question 3: We are all like letters without stamps. We come back in every birth. The stamp for Akshardham is not available anywhere, so will we get the stamp for Akshardham?
"Yes, you will," Swamishri said firmly.
Immediately a question arising from this answer was asked: "We ask this again and again; don't you get bored?"
Swamishri said in a lilting voice with great feeling, "This is seva. Why would I be bored?"
Just as a merchant is not troubled by a customer's repeated enquiries, so Swamishri, the giver of moksha, does not tire of such questions asked again and again by spiritual seekers.
Question 4: We feel sleepy in the assembly, because it seems the same talk is being given again and again. So please explain the glory of the assembly.

Swamishri answered with a question. Swamishri said, "Do you have a shop or not? Do the same customers come or new ones? Do they ask for the same things or new ones? Don't you get bored there? Yet there you open the shop at 7.30 in the morning instead of 8.00. You have not understood the talk of satsang, so you get bored. If you understand it, there is joy and joy."
Question 5: We are all jivas and you are Aksharbrahman. This distinction is eternal. So have we met for the very first time?
"Yes. For the first time. We have never met before. And it is only because Bhagwan showed grace that we have met," said Swamishri.
